note:
ISO 2026-W05 runs from January 26 through February 1. Mars and Pluto are separated by about 1.5° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mercury and Venus are separated by about 1.6° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌓 First Quarter — 04:47:23 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Mintaka, Arneb, Alnilam, Phact, Alnitak, Saiph, Wazn, Betelgeuse, Menkalinan as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -10.1; direct motion; 47.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Opposition in ecliptic longitude Feb 01 22:09 UTC. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Jan 31 03:18 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Jan 27 16:42 UTC. Mercury: In solar glare; magnitude -1.4; direct motion; 99.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Venus in ecliptic longitude Jan 29 10:17 UTC. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 99.7% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mercury in ecliptic longitude Jan 29 10:17 UTC. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.1; direct motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Pluto in ecliptic longitude Jan 27 23:01 UTC. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 97.4% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.6; retrograde motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Jan 31 03:18 UTC. Saturn: Naked eye; magnitude 1.0; direct motion; 99.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.7; retrograde motion; 99.9% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Jan 27 16:42 UTC. Neptune: Telescope; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: In solar glare; magnitude 14.5; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Mars in ecliptic longitude Jan 27 23:01 UTC.

**Binoculars:** Trace Dorado’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Dor at its charted position. Trace Pictor’s charted figure in the finder, then identify β Pic at its charted position.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on Crab Nebula, Great Nebula in Orion, De Mairan's Nebula, M36, M78, M37. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

descriptors.name: Full Moon
descriptors.summary: Astronomical lunar phase near opposition to the Sun.
descriptors.body: Full Moon is the lunar phase in which the Moon and Sun are approximately opposite in geocentric ecliptic longitude, so the lunar disk is fully illuminated as seen from Earth.
